items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: I told them the reason and all and they knew I should have gone from Nazarro long ago... Some people trying to get us to break up that act from him long ago. I wouldn't break it up.

ctx.x: I said it was amazing that you could have somebody on your back for so many years -- Nazarro.
I heard you. I know what you're going to say. See, Nazarro is Jewish but the point I'm trying to bring out to

it, you see, the Jewish people are very clannish, they stick together, you know. If you told a Jewish friend over there how rotten I was, he'd take your word for it, you understand? More so than he would take somebody else's word saying I was good and the other person was a different nationality. But the person who's Jewish and said to the other Jew. He says, you know this guy, he's terrible. Don't trust him. That's all he needs to say. Now get the Jew that says he don't know what he's talking about, get the Jew…

items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Trick had introduced Buck and Bubbles, two boys that he met at Carnegie Hall

ctx.x: So it comes down for us to get ready to go on the stage to do the concert, Sunday concert at this Columbia Theater, I heard the manager and Nazarro talking about he don't want no niggers in the theater, didn't want no niggers on the stage. I heard him talk about that. But they don't know I hear 'em. I'm off stage and hear this. And he tells him he's going to bring us on in his act -- no, he didn't want us in the theater -- on the stage. So, when they comes to arguing the point, I'm going to tell Buck when they…

and manage the theater and I will take care of my act. And I start up the stairs to tell Buck about it. Something says, don't tell him. Then I go on back and wait for the time for us to go on and Mr. Trick had introduced Buck and Bubbles, two boys that he met at Carnegie Hall and asked him would he give them a job in the theater, so he thought he'd bring us along. One plays the flute in 14 feet of rice pudding. Are the gentlemen there? Their names are Buck and Bubbles.

So we walk on the stage in vagabond dress, yella shoes, brown pants, blue coat, brown cap and gray cap. And we walk on, the audience had a big "Oh," and we start off. The first song we did was "Rhythm For Sale." After "Rhythm For Sale" I did another song, can't think of the name of it. However, he says, "Bubbles, I'd like for you to tell the audience about the letter that you got from your mother." Now I had never told Buck about what had happened before we went on concerning

items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: No, not Nazarro -- Nat Nazarro and his company. He had a boy, understand that worked with him.

ctx.x: after New York we went to Canada and from Canada we went again to the Loews circuit throughout New York. Then we had the difficulty with the contract in the year of 1926 and '25.
Initially, Buck and Bubbles were performing with the Nat Nazarro Brothers?

No, not Nazarro -- Nat Nazarro and his company. He had a boy, understand that worked with him. He had an understand that worked with him, there were no brothers. He hired a little fella that he could pick up and throw up and down to do a Hawaian trick or flag him up, he'd do tricks. I never seen anything like that. Well, that's what he had. They weren't brothers. He hired this little fella as an act to work with him on the stage. That's who he had working with him.
